title: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: Terminal 5 and Tuas Port
sections.summary: Terminal 5 is being built larger than several existing terminals combined, and Tuas Mega Port is expanding in phases, expected to fully complete in the 2040s.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: In terms of hard infrastructure, a colossal Terminal 5 (T5) is being built, larger than several of our existing terminals combined and the Tuas Mega Port is expanding in phases, with full completion expected in the 2040s.

sections.label: Assurance on major project demand
sections.summary: The passage asks how confident we are that T5, Tuas Port and other major projects meet lasting real demand and what mechanisms adjust pace, scope and costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: How confident are we that T5, Tuas Port and other major projects are being built to meet lasting real demand?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: What assurance do we have that these assets will remain relevant to the region and the world by the time construction completes?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: And what mechanisms are in place to adjust project pace, scope and costs as global macro conditions evolve, so as to minimise fiscal and strategic risk?

sections.label: Status of T5 and Tuas
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry can update the House on the current status of T5 and the Tuas port development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry update the House on the current status of T5 and the Tuas port development?

sections.label: Heavy investment in public transport
sections.summary: Heavy investment in public transport, including expanding the MRT network and upgrading buses, has boosted capacity and improved connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Heavy investment in public transport – expanding the Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) network, modernising trains and signalling, upgrading bus fleets and developing integrated transport hubs just to name a few – has boosted capacity and improved connectivity.

sections.label: Plans for land transport system
sections.summary: The passage asks what concrete plans MOT is implementing for a more reliable, user-centric, inclusive and safer land transport system meeting changing commuter needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Regardless of on foot or on wheels, commuters expect more choice, faster first‑mile and last‑mile connections, and a system that is safe, inclusive and resilient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask what concrete plans is MOT implementing to build a more reliable, user-centric, inclusive and safer land transport system that meets these changing commuter needs?

sections.label: Supporting greener smarter mobility infrastructure
sections.summary: The passage asks what MOT is doing to boost capacity, availability and reliability of supporting infrastructure such as EV charging and AV-ready roadside systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: In support of greener, smarter mobility, what is MOT doing to boost the capacity, availability and reliability of supporting infrastructure, ranging from EV charging networks, grid readiness, interoperable payment and telematics standards, and AV‑ready roadside systems?

sections.label: COE and AV adoption
sections.summary: Asks how MOT expects AV adoption to affect medium- to long-term design of the COE system and other ownership controls.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) is a critical policy lever used to manage car population and road demand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: How does MOT anticipate AV adoption affect the medium‑ to long‑term design of the COE system and other ownership controls?

sections.label: T5 and Changi East build
sections.summary: Describes the scale of T5 and Changi East Urban District, listing added passenger and cargo capacity and related industrial and connectivity projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, if we take a step back and imagine and examine the scale of what is being built at T5, including the Changi East Urban District, this is not merely an airport expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This is economic architecture, with T5 adding capacity of 15 million passengers annually, and the Changi East Industrial Zone expanding cargo from three to 5.4 million tonnes annually, complemented by Airport Logistics Park 2, Tampines Logistics Park, Changi South, Pasir Ris, Wafer Fab Park, Seletar Aerospace Park, the maintenance, repair and operations (MRO) operations in Changi and in Loyang, and enhanced connectivity via the Loyang Viaduct.

sections.label: Changi East aerotropolis vision
sections.summary: States the Changi East Urban District must become an aerotropolis integrating MRO, sustainable fuels, digital services and AI logistics, with wider connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The Changi East Urban District must evolve into a next generation aerotropolis, integrating advanced MRO, sustainable aviation fuels, digital aviation services and AI-driven logistics command centres linked with Changi Business Park and Loyang Industrial Estate, this becomes a seamless innovation to production to export corridor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Connectivity must also extend beyond air to the Tanah Merah ferry terminal and integration with the Johor Singapore Special Economic Zone and Batam-Bintan-Karimun Free Trade Zone.

sections.label: Aviation and maritime manpower
sections.summary: Asks whether air and sea connectivity growth is matched by manpower, local pipelines for higher value roles, and progress of two talent programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: First, with expanding air and sea connectivity, are we keeping pace with manpower needs in aviation and maritime, and building a strong local pipeline for higher value roles?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: And also, what progress have the One Aviation Manpower Programme and Maritime Cluster Fund made in attracting and developing talent?

sections.label: T5 Changi capacity increase
sections.summary: States Changi Airport will add 50 million passengers per annum in capacity when T5 is ready around the middle of next decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Changi Airport will increase its capacity by another 50 million passengers per annum when T5 is ready around the middle of next decade.

sections.label: One Aviation Manpower Fund
sections.summary: States that in July 2025 CAAS announced a 200 million One Aviation Manpower Fund to attract, develop and retain the aviation workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In July 2025, the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) announced a 200 million One Aviation Manpower Fund to attract, develop and retain the aviation workforce.

sections.label: Women in aviation workforce
sections.summary: Today, only about 20% of the aviation sector workforce are women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Today, only about 20% of the workforce in the aviation sector are women.

sections.label: Liability in malfunction or incident
sections.summary: It asks where liability lies in the event of a malfunction or incident.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In the event of a malfunction or incident, where does liability lie?

sections.label: Embracing technology without disrupting livelihoods
sections.summary: It urges operators to work with unions in the tripartite framework to co-create fair AV career pathways and support workers through the transition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: As I had earlier highlighted in my Budget debate clarifications, while it is important for us to embrace new technologies, this must be done in a way that does not disrupt livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I therefore urge operators to work closely with our unions within our tripartite framework to co-create fair AV career pathways and ensure workers are supported through this transition.

sections.label: Autonomous vehicle trials and buses
sections.summary: In 2026, a small number of vehicles are in trials in Punggol, and LTA plans to procure six autonomous buses from mid-2026 for three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Today, in 2026, a small number of vehicles are now involved in trials in the residential district in Punggol and the Land Transport Authority (LTA) plans to procure six autonomous buses with operations beginning in mid-2026 for an initial period of three years.

sections.label: Dubai and Saudi autonomy targets
sections.summary: Dubai aims for 25% of total transportation to be autonomous by 2030, and Saudi Arabia targets 25% of goods transport vehicles fully autonomous by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Dubai Autonomous Transportation Strategy aims to have 25% of the total transportation in Dubai to be autonomous by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Saudi Arabia's Transport General Authority has set a target for 25% of all goods transport vehicles to be fully autonomous by 2030.

sections.label: Singapore charging points count
sections.summary: In response to a February Parliamentary Question, Singapore currently has around 28,300 charging points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In response to my Parliamentary Question in February this year, I understand that Singapore currently has around 28,300 charging points.

sections.label: Electric car registrations share
sections.summary: Of all cars registered in 2025, 45% are already electric.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Of all cars registered in 2025, 45% are already electric.

sections.label: Mature estate chargers and idling fees
sections.summary: Asks when MOT will commit to a mature estate fast-charge mandate and how it will mandate idling fees across public charging operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Residents in newer BTOs often have more access to higher-power chargers, but many mature estates remain stuck with slow 7.4 kW chargers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: When will MOT commit to a "mature estate fast-charge" mandate to ensure residents in older estates including in some parts of Hougang, are not left behind?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: And finally, how will MOT intend to mandate "idling fees" across all public charging operators to prevent lot-hogging?

sections.label: Fast chargers in HDB estates
sections.summary: Urges LTA to deploy more fast chargers in HDB estates, especially at convenient high-traffic locations, for P2P and commercial drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: While the roll-out of slow chargers in HDB car parks has supported convenient overnight charging, many EV users, particularly P2P users as well as commercial drivers, require access to fast daytime charging infrastructure in the daytime so as to sustain their operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I therefore urge LTA to spearhead the deployment of more fast chargers within the HDB estates, especially at convenient and high-traffic locations, such as near food establishments and neighbourhood centres.

sections.label: Summonses for missing lights
sections.summary: Between 2023 and 2025, 167 summonses were issued for missing lights, mostly on roads, not footpaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Between 2023 and 2025, 167 summonses were issued for missing lights, but these were mostly on roads, not footpaths.

sections.label: Hougang Avenue 3 bridge lifts
sections.summary: Recounts lift installation at four Hougang Avenue 3 overhead bridges, with works now tentatively starting in the third quarter of 2027.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In February 2023, I asked a Parliamentary Question about when lifts would be installed at overhead bridges along Hougang Avenue 3.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Then Transport Minister, Mr S Iswaran, affirmed that the number of seniors and commuters with mobility challenges would be a consideration for prioritisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He further confirmed that four of the bridges along Hougang Avenue 3 would be prioritised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The next incumbent Transport Minister, Mr Chee Hong Tat, identified the overhead bridges at Blocks 101, 172, 241 and 248 as the four being prioritised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He stated that construction works for that phase of LTA's retrofitting works were scheduled to take place progressively from the fourth quarter of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Based on the latest indications from LTA's consultants to our Town Council, the lift works will only commence tentatively in the third quarter of 2027.

sections.label: Parc Vera covered walkway petition
sections.summary: In July 2025, 176 Parc Vera Condominium residents petitioned for an 80-metre covered walkway linking its rear side gate to an existing HDB covered linkway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: In July 2025, 176 residents at Parc Vera Condominium at Hougang Street 32, submitted a petition for 80 metres covered walkway linking its rear side gate to an existing HDB covered linkway.

sections.label: LTA and Town Council limits
sections.summary: LTA does not entertain last-mile connectivity requests outside 800 metres of an MRT station or 400 metres of a bus interchange, and Town Councils cannot fund projects not primarily benefiting HDB residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: The LTA does not entertain requests for its last-mile connectivity plans if they fall outside 800 metres of a MRT station or 400 metres of a bus interchange and not along a MRT managed road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Lastly, the Town Council has no jurisdiction to spend funds on projects that do not primarily benefit HDB residents.

sections.label: Developer sheltered connectivity mandate
sections.summary: The passage asks whether URA and LTA can mandate at planning permission stage that developers provide sheltered connectivity to public transport nodes, including covered access from condominium side gates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Can URA and LTA mandate at the planning permission stage that developers provide sheltered connectivity to the nearest public transport nodes, including such covered access from each condominium side gates, or include this in the development control handbooks to guide developers on ensuring upfront connectivity by design?

sections.label: Inclusive buses and trains measures
sections.summary: The passage asks what further measures are planned to make buses and trains more inclusive for young families and persons with disabilities, and whether ramp deployment SOPs can be standardised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share what further measures are planned to make buses and trains more inclusive for young families and persons with disabilities?

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And can standard operational procedures (SOPs) on ramp deployment be standardised across operators alongside a public education effort?

sections.label: Land Transport Master Plan 2040 target
sections.summary: The Land Transport Master Plan 2040 sets a target of nine in 10 peak public transport journeys completed within 45 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, the Land Transport Master Plan 2040 sets an ambitious target of nine in 10 peak public transport journeys completed within 45 minutes.

sections.label: Express rail on Seletar Line
sections.summary: The passage urges the Government to include express rail services on the Seletar Line from the outset, with bypass tracks at non-interchange suburban stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Infrastructure of this scale does not just serve demand, it will generate it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge the Government to incorporate provisions for express rail services on the Seletar Line from the outset, specifically, bypass tracks at non-interchange suburban stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Bypass tracks would allow us to serve every major underserved catchment along the line's alignment – Simpang and Yishun East, Seletar and Jalan Kayu, Whampoa and the greater Southern Waterfront – with local trains while express services overtake local services at these stations to reach downtown core at speed.

sections.label: Johor RTS opening
sections.summary: The Rapid Transit System to Johor is expected to open by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, by the end of this year, the Rapid Transit System (RTS) to Johor is expected to open.

sections.label: Woodlands Thomson-East Coast Line peak services
sections.summary: Asks about LTA's plans for smooth, accessible public transport for Woodlands residents using the Thomson-East Coast Line to town at peak periods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: What are LTA's plans to ensure that Singaporeans staying at Woodlands and using the Thomson-East Coast Line to head down to town during peak periods can continue to enjoy smooth and accessible public transport services?

sections.label: Circle Line Stage 6 opening dates
sections.summary: Asks whether Circle Line Stage 6 will open in the second quarter and whether Thomson-East Coast and Downtown lines meet at Sungei Bedok in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: First, may I ask whether the Circle Line Stage 6, linking HarbourFront to Marina Bay via Keppel, Cantonment and Prince Edward Road stations will open in the second quarter of this year, as earlier announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Second, can the Minister confirm that the Thomson-East Coast Line and the Downtown Line will meet at Sungei Bedok station through Xilin and Bedok South stations in the second half of 2026, which is this year?

sections.label: JRL timeline, bus link, rail reliability
sections.summary: Asks if the Ministry will commit resources if timelines are at risk, urges a new bus service for JRL access, and notes Rail Reliability Taskforce recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: If the timelines are at risk, will the Ministry commit the necessary resources to keep the project on schedule so that hundreds of thousands of residents can benefit as planned?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: There is no direct bus link, including for students of Juying Secondary School.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: I urge MOT to introduce a new bus service under the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme so that residents, students and workers can fully benefit from the JRL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Chairman, the Rail Reliability Taskforce has set out clear recommendations – accelerate renewal of ageing core systems, including train signalling and traction power, strengthen backup and resilience measures, improve asset management and spare part planning, deepen workforce capabilities and enhance commuter communications during disruptions.

sections.label: Ageing network renewal and upgrading
sections.summary: States that with parts of the network ageing, including lines, assets and equipment, renewal and upgrading works will intensify.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: With parts of our network ageing, including lines, assets and equipment, renewal and upgrading works will intensify.

sections.label: Harmonised rail training and manpower package
sections.summary: States harmonised training gives rail workers portable skills across lines, systems and operators, and asks for updates on the 2019 Rail Manpower Development Package extension.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Harmonised training will help ensure that rail workers develop portable skills – skills that can be applied across different lines, systems and operators – strengthening both operational resilience and workers' long-term employability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: I would also like to ask for updates on the extension of the 2019 $100 million Rail Manpower Development Package.

sections.label: Rail new entrant basic salaries
sections.summary: States starting basic salaries for new entrants remain around $2,250 monthly, with advertised gross pay often depending on overtime structurally tied to the trade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Yet today, starting basic salaries for new entrants remain around $2,250 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: While advertised gross pay may range between $3,000 to $4,000 and beyond, a significant portion still depends on overtime, and this high overtime is actually structurally tied to this trade.

sections.label: Electric public bus fleet target
sections.summary: Half of the public bus fleet is expected to be electric by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Looking ahead, half of our public bus fleet is expected to be electric by 2030.

sections.label: Bus connectivity in Flora Estate
sections.summary: Flora Estate is served by two bus services along Flora Road and one along Flora Drive, with low off-peak frequency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Let us begin with bus connectivity in Flora Estate, a dense residential estate in the northeastern corner of Singapore, served by only two bus services along Flora Road and one along Flora Drive, with relatively low frequency, especially during off-peak hours.

sections.label: Temporary lane closure delay simulations
sections.summary: LTA shared that upcoming temporary lane closures simulations show delays of up to nine minutes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: LTA has shared that upcoming temporary lane closures simulations shows that it could result in delays of up to nine minutes.

sections.label: Accidents at Loyang Avenue junction
sections.summary: Thirteen accidents were recorded along Loyang Avenue at its junction with Old Tampines Road between 2023 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Along Loyang Avenue, 13 accidents were recorded between 2023 and 2025 at its junction with Old Tampines Road.

sections.label: Infrastructure works impact on residents
sections.summary: Residents in Pasir Ris and Loyang face noise and dust from infrastructure works, with complaints nearly tripling to about 230 cases per year compared to 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Even as we build for long-term improvements, like the Loyang Viaduct and Cross-Island Line, residents in Pasir Ris and Loyang live with the immediate costs of infrastructure works, like noise and dust, with complaints in the region nearly tripling to about 230 cases per year as compared to 2023.

sections.label: Enforcement checks at ports of entry
sections.summary: The passage asks how enforcement checks at ports of entry have stepped up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: How have enforcement checks at our ports of entry stepped up?

sections.label: Road pricing demand management
sections.summary: Road pricing has managed demand effectively but raises business and household costs and cannot be the only lever.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Road pricing has been effective in managing demand, but it raises business and household costs, and it cannot be our only lever.

sections.label: Malaysian motorcycles entering Singapore
sections.summary: About 69,000 Malaysian-registered motorcycles enter Singapore daily in 2025, with 22,000 traffic offences and 1,600 accidents, causing peak-hour congestion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: On average, about 69,000 Malaysian-registered motorcycles enter Singapore daily in 2025, with quite a significant number issued with traffic offences, about 22,000 of them, and some involved in accidents, about 1,600, based on a Parliamentary Question that I filed recently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: While these riders contribute to our economy, concentrated peak-hour inflows have been causing congestions along corridors, such as the Bukit Timah Expressway and Pan-Island Expressway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Can I ask if the Ministry have conducted studies on the impact of cross-border motorcycles on traffic flows and are there targeted traffic management measures to manage peak in-flows?

sections.label: Traffic management technology suggestions
sections.summary: Suggestions include integrating real-time GPS data from vehicles and buses, predictive modelling, and corridor-wide synchronisation for smoother green waves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Some of the suggestions include, integrate real-time GPS data from vehicles and buses, use predictive modelling to anticipate build-ups before they occur and implement corridor-wide synchronisation to create smoother "green waves"?

sections.label: Singapore road safety record
sections.summary: Singapore's roads are among the safest globally, reflecting decades of investment in infrastructure, enforcement and education, with year-on-year declines in fatality rates per capita.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Chairman, the roads in Singapore are among the safest globally and that reflects decades of investment in infrastructure, enforcement and education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Recent figures show year-on-year declines in fatality rates per capita.

sections.label: Vision Zero and MOT initiatives
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOT considered a tailored Vision Zero approach and what new educational or behavioural initiatives it plans, and will speak on ERP 2.0, COE and car ownership accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Vision Zero frameworks adopted in parts of Europe and North America, for example, emphasise system design that anticipates human error while reducing its consequences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I therefore ask the Minister, has MOT considered adopting elements of a Vision Zero approach tailored to Singapore, where system design, speed management and clear accountability align across all road users?

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, while engineering and enforcement remain vital, what new educational or behavioural initiatives are MOT planning that go beyond conventional campaigns to foster mutual road user respect?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I will speak on three areas: one, ERP 2.0 resulting in increasing of vehicular supply; two, refreshing the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) system for greater equity; and three, accessibility in car ownership in our next phase of land transport policy.

sections.label: COE category vehicle classification
sections.summary: Manufacturers adjust specifications so premium models qualify under Cat A while practical vehicles like the Toyota Noah Hybrid fall under Cat B.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Manufacturers are adjusting specifications, whether engine power or motor design, so that premium models qualify under Category A (Cat A), while practical vehicles end up in Category B (Cat B) due to technical criteria, even though they are not luxury vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For instance, the Toyota Noah Hybrid, with an open market value (OMV) of around $28,000 falls under Cat B.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, a luxury model like the BMW 216 Gran Coupe, with an OMV of around $35,000 falls under Cat A.

sections.label: COE framework evolution proposal
sections.summary: The COE framework could evolve from separate Cat A and Cat B categories towards an OMV-based model with a single bidding pool.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Building on this, the COE framework could evolve from separate Cat A and Cat B categories towards an OMV-based model with a single bidding pool.

sections.label: COE quota projection versus actual
sections.summary: Chee Hong Tat said COE quota for Categories A, B and C would rise each quarter, but LTA's February to April 2026 quota is lower than the last quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: In November 2024, then Minister for Transport, Mr Chee Hong Tat, informed this House that with the planned injection of 20,000 additional COEs over the next few years, the COE quota for Category A, B and C would continue to rise each quarter, before reaching its projected peak supply from 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: However, the recent announcement by LTA shows that the COE quota for February to April 2026 is in fact lower than the last quarter.

sections.label: Cat A and Cat B COE prices
sections.summary: Cat A COEs fell and Cat B COEs rose for February to April 2026, narrowing the price gap to $4,570, the smallest in 58 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: In addition, we observe that the number of Cat A COEs has fallen for the February to April 2026 period, while the supply of Cat B COEs has increased compared to the previous quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: It is therefore not surprising that in the first bidding exercise of February 2026, the price gap between a Cat A and Cat B COE narrowed sharply to $4,570, the smallest gap in 58 months, since March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: In the second bidding exercise of February, Cat A COE price was even higher than the Cat B COE price by $1,500.

sections.label: COE on motorcycles questioned
sections.summary: Imposing the COE on motorcycles seems illogical as they do not significantly contribute to traffic congestion, with over 60,000 crossing the Causeway daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, imposing the COE on a motorcycle seems illogical, as they do not significantly contribute to traffic congestion in the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is noteworthy that approximately more than 60,000 motorcycles cross the Causeway daily to commute and work in Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore re-elected to ICAO and IMO
sections.summary: Singapore was re-elected to both ICAO and IMO Councils with the highest number of votes in our categories.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Singapore was re-elected to both ICAO and IMO Councils with the highest number of votes in our categories.

sections.label: Terminal 5 construction and capacity
sections.summary: Construction on T5 started last year and should be completed by the mid-2030s, increasing Changi's capacity by about 50 million passengers per year.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Construction on T5 started last year and should be completed by the mid-2030s.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: As Ms Poh Li San noted, this will increase Changi’s capacity by about 50 million passengers per year.

sections.label: Tuas Port berths opening
sections.summary: The 12th berth at Tuas Port opened last year and four more berths will open this year.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)

sections.label: JRL West Coast Extension studies

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: So, I am happy to announce that from 1 April, we will open up rides for interested members of the public.

sections.label: Autonomous public bus trials

sentences.text: LTA will launch trials for autonomous public buses by the second half of this year via bus service 400 in Marina Bay and bus service 191 in One-North.

sections.label: Public feedback on transport

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Over the last three months, LTA has met more than 200 people for in-person Focus Group Discussions and received more than 3,500 written responses from the public.

sections.label: Narrowing public transport time gap

sentences.text: Today, public transport may take two to three times as long as private transport, often from areas where there are only bus connections, but no MRT.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: I want to narrow this gap to be closer to one to two times.

sections.label: Commuters shifting off peak
sections.summary: Around 8% of commuters have shifted off peak, making morning peak rides less crowded for other commuters.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Around 8% of commuters have shifted off peak, which has resulted in a less crowded ride for other commuters travelling during morning peak hours.

sections.label: Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme results
sections.summary: Since the $1 billion Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme launched, 25 new bus services were added and over 60 existing ones enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Since the $1 billion Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme was launched, we have added 25 new bus services and enhanced over 60 existing ones islandwide.

sections.label: Malaysian motorcycle volume measures
sections.summary: The Vehicle Entry Permit fee rise from $4 to $7 and the 2027 RTS Link are expected to reduce foreign motorcycle numbers.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: But to Mr Liang Eng Hwa's question, we are watching the volume of Malaysian motorcycles very closely.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We expect the increase in the Vehicle Entry Permit fee from $4 to $7 per day and the opening of the RTS Link, from 2027, to reduce the volume of the foreign motorcycle population in Singapore.

sections.label: COE categorisation review
sections.summary: LTA is asked to review COE categorisation for cars, gathering public and industry views, including a proposal on open market value discounts or surcharges.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Last month, Category A prices exceeded Category B prices, although in the exercise that just concluded an hour ago, Category B has returned to somewhat normal, higher than Category A once again.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: But with Category A quota supply having peaked last year and Category B quota supply continuing to increase this year, it is likely that the two prices will continue to converge for some time.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: I have therefore asked LTA to review this issue.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We will gather views from the public and from the industry on how to improve the COE categorisation for cars, including Mr Chia's specific proposal to apply discounts or surcharges based on open market value.

sections.label: Route adjustment found possible

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: After further analysis, LTA found that it was indeed possible to adjust the route.

sections.label: Flights suspended to Middle East

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Singapore Airlines and Scoot have suspended their flights to affected Middle Eastern destinations until 7 March.

sections.label: Aviation jobs created
sections.summary: Growth has created over 60,000 quality jobs directly in aviation, including air traffic controllers and engineers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Our growth thus far has also created over 60,000 quality jobs directly in aviation, from air traffic controllers managing our busy skies to engineers managing our aircrafts.

sections.label: OneAviation Manpower Fund commitment
sections.summary: CAAS has committed $200 million towards the OneAviation Manpower Fund to attract, develop and retain the OneAviation workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: CAAS has committed $200 million towards the OneAviation Manpower Fund to attract, develop and retain the OneAviation workforce.

sentences.text: Today, upon graduation, Rui Qi will still need to undergo up to 44 months of professional training before attaining a professional license from CAAS to become a licensed aircraft engineer.

sections.label: Women in ATCO workforce
sections.summary: About 40% of the ATCO workforce are women today, and this share has been growing steadily.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: About 40% of our ATCO workforce are women today, and this has been growing steadily.

sections.label: Women In Aviation mentorship

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Women In Aviation Singapore Chapter’s mentorship programme has supported over 100 mentees over the past four years.

sections.label: Punggol shuttle trial ridership

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In Punggol, around 740 people have tried the shuttles on Routes 1 and 3.

sections.label: Public rides on Routes 1 and 3
sections.summary: Given positive feedback, rides on Routes 1 and 3 will open to the public from 1 April.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Given the positive feedback, we will open up the rides on Routes 1 and 3 to the public from 1 April.

sections.label: Flat fare for shuttle routes
sections.summary: From the middle of this year, commuters may board and alight at any stop along Routes 1 and 3 at a flat $4 fare.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: From the middle of this year, commuters may board and alight at any stop along Routes 1 and 3 at a flat fare of $4 per passenger.

sections.label: EV share of new cars

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In January 2026, EV adoption grew to a record 55% of new car registrations.

sections.label: Fast charger deployment numbers

sentences.text: Mr Ang Wei Neng and Mr Dennis Tan suggested deploying more fast chargers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We have already deployed 150 fast charging points at 70 carparks at HDB town centres and JTC premises.

sections.label: Fast-charging hubs per HDB town
sections.summary: At least one fast-charging hub with at least six fast charging points will be deployed per HDB town by end of next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Currently, there are fast-charging hubs in commercial and industrial premises, such as Pasir Ris Mall, Suntec City and Corporation Place in Jurong West.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will deploy more fast-charging hubs so that there will be at least one fast-charging hub per HDB town by the end of next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Each hub will be equipped with at least six fast charging points.

sections.label: National EV Safety Specialist Certification
sections.summary: The National EV Safety Specialist Certification launched in 2022 has given over 2,000 people foundational EV maintenance safety training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Mr Ang Wei Neng and Ms Yeo Wan Ling highlighted the importance of equipping our workforce for the EV transition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We launched the National EV Safety Specialist Certification in 2022, which has provided more than 2,000 people with foundational safety training in EV maintenance.

sections.label: Ban on ferrying workers in caged lorries
sections.summary: From 1 January 2027, ferrying of workers in caged lorries will no longer be allowed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: From 1 January 2027, we will no longer allow the ferrying of workers in caged lorries.

sections.label: Caged lorries for goods transport
sections.summary: Companies may still use caged lorries for goods, or replace the cage with a canopy, side railings and rain covers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Companies may still use their caged lorries to transport goods.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: If companies need the flexibility to transport either workers or goods on their rear decks, they can choose to replace the cage structure with a canopy, side railings and rain covers.

sections.label: Friendly Streets pilot site speeds
sections.summary: At the five pilot sites with Friendly Streets, average vehicular speeds reduced by up to 25%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In the five pilot sites with Friendly Streets, we have seen average vehicular speeds reducing by up to 25%.

sections.label: Rolling out 20 Friendly Streets
sections.summary: Another 20 new Friendly Streets will be rolled out over the next few years, given positive feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Given the positive feedback, we will roll out another 20 new Friendly Streets over the next few years.

sections.label: Friendly Street in every town

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: By 2030, every town will have at least one Friendly Street.

sections.label: Sea as Singapore's passage
sections.summary: The sea is described as Singapore's open passage to the world, with sea lanes and ports of call affected by disruptions and tensions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the sea has always been Singapore's open passage to the world.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: When we speak of supply chain disruptions, it is sea lanes that grant or prohibit, passage to supply chains across the world.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: When we speak of geopolitical tensions, it is the literal ports of call that are changing amid greater volatility and global uncertainties.

sections.label: Land Transport Master Plan consultation
sections.summary: LTA has launched a nationwide public consultation to refresh the Land Transport Master Plan 2040.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As the Acting Minister mentioned, LTA has launched a nationwide public consultation to refresh the Land Transport Master Plan 2040.

sections.label: Expanding Friendly Streets to all towns
sections.summary: Friendly Streets will be expanded to all towns by 2030, as shared by Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling has shared, we will be expanding Friendly Streets to all towns by 2030.

sections.label: Covered linkways radius extended
sections.summary: Covered linkways within a 400-metre radius of MRT stations are now extended to an 800-metre radius at Friendly Streets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: For example, we already have covered linkways within a 400-metre radius of MRT stations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: This is now extended to an 800-metre radius at our Friendly Streets.

sections.label: Bridge upgrading phase works
sections.summary: Over 100 bridges are being upgraded in this phase, with works at two bridges starting by mid-2027 and the other two later.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The four bridges mentioned by Ms Lim is in this current phase, which commenced at the end of last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: There are over 100 bridges that we are upgrading in this phase.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will commence works at two of the bridges mentioned by Ms Lim by the middle of 2027 before moving on to the other two bridges later.

sections.label: Foldable seats in bays
sections.summary: LTA will install foldable seats within the bays where feasible to mitigate this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: To mitigate this, LTA will install foldable seats within the bays where feasible.

sections.label: Wheelchairs and strollers in bus bays
sections.summary: From April 2026, bus captains on around 10 selected services will facilitate wheelchair and open stroller use of bays first-come-first-serve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: From April 2026, on around 10 selected bus services plying routes that serve more wheelchair or mobility aid users and parents with young children, our bus captains will facilitate the use of bays by wheelchairs and open strollers on a first-come-first-serve basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Depending on the findings, we will consider making this the norm across the entire network.

sections.label: LTA and SBS Transit deployment
sections.summary: LTA will work with SBS Transit to deploy this initiative at more locations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: LTA will work with SBS Transit to deploy this initiative at more locations.

sections.label: Priority queue lines setup
sections.summary: Priority queue lines will be set up at priority boarding doors in MRT stations and at lifts in public transport nodes progressively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: First, we will clearly set up priority queue lines at the priority boarding doors within MRT stations and at the lifts within our public transport nodes progressively.

sections.label: Lights on public paths
sections.summary: Bicycles, power-assisted bicycles and personal mobility devices must display a front white light and rear red light when ridden in darkness from 7.00 pm to 7.00 am.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: On the requirement of lights, bicycles, power-assisted bicycles and personal mobility devices must display a front white light and a rear red light when ridden on public paths and roads during hours of darkness between 7.00 pm and 7.00 am.

sections.label: Pedestrians on cycling paths
sections.summary: There is no plan to prohibit pedestrians from using cycling paths adjacent to Pedestrian-Only Paths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: On whether to prohibit pedestrians from walking on cycling paths when a dedicated alternative is provided, this had been deliberated before.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We do not plan to prohibit pedestrians from using cycling paths adjacent to Pedestrian-Only Paths.

sections.label: Land Transport Master Plan consultation
sections.summary: A year-long public consultation to update the Land Transport Master Plan began in November last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Since November last year, we have embarked on a year-long public consultation to update the Land Transport Master Plan with the aim of exploring different commuting needs together and jointly shaping our future transport system.

sections.label: Pilot for strollers on buses
sections.summary: A pilot programme starts in April on about 10 bus routes to help parents with strollers and wheelchair-bound passengers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We also understand the difficulty faced by many parents travelling on public buses with strollers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Therefore, we will implement a pilot programme starting in April this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: On approximately 10 bus routes, bus captains will help parents with strollers and wheelchair-bound passengers with the use of the designated spaces, on a first-come, first-serve basis.

sections.label: COE review and POB lifts
sections.summary: The COE review starts immediately, with consultation over the rest of the year as part of the Land Transport Master Plan process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: For the COE review, I intend to start this immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We will have to take the rest of the year to do the consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We will take it as part of the Land Transport Master Plan process as Minister of State Baey has explained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Hopefully, by the end of this year, we ought to have some form of conclusion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Infrastructure like pedestrian overhead bridge (POB) lifts, as mentioned, we are in this current phase with more than 100 POB lifts.

sections.label: COE supply increase commitment
sections.summary: The question asks whether MOT remains committed to increasing overall COE supply by 20,000 as announced in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Is MOT still committed to increasing the overall COE supply by 20,000 as announced in 2024?

sections.label: Injecting additional COEs
sections.summary: Plans remain to inject up to 20,000 additional COEs over the next few years, based on reasons that stay valid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Chairman, we have plans to inject up to 20,000 additional COEs over the next few years, as Mr Ang has pointed out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: It was on the premise that the total mileage has fallen and our ability to manage congestion using ERP 2.0 will be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: So, those reasons stay valid; we will continue to inject those COEs over the next few years.

sections.label: Government bus network subsidies
sections.summary: The Government provides a billion dollars yearly in subsidies to the bus network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Overall, on a yearly basis, the Government puts in a billion dollars as subsidies into the bus network.

sections.label: ERP as last response
sections.summary: ERP is used only when really necessary, as gantries were hard and expensive to build.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: For the most part, ERP is always our last response, not least because ERP 1.0 gantries were hard to build and expensive to build; but even with ERP 2.0, I would like to reassure the Member that we would use road pricing only when it is really necessary.

sections.label: Highway jam and accident clearance
sections.summary: Clearing jams or accidents on the highway takes an average of about 15 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Today, they take about an average of 15 minutes to clear jams or clear an accident on the highway and to then allow traffic to continue smoothly.

sections.label: HDB car park charging points
sections.summary: Baseline deployment is at least three charging points per HDB car park, achieved in 90% of car parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: One of the key feedback that we often get is that the additional charging lots is subject to power capacity and it just does not seem to be the case that we might get twelve in each multi-storey car park in the near term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We started with a baseline deployment of at least three charging points per HDB car park.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And I have shared in my earlier reply that 90% of our car parks have achieved this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I wanted to take the opportunity to talk about how we are sequencing our fast-charging hubs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I had mentioned that we will be looking at having one in each HDB town, and this will be relying on existing spare capacity at car parks where possible, and for future tranches of deployment, we are also working with the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), and the Energy Market Authority (EMA) to optimise our electrical grid to minimise costly grid upgrades.

sections.label: OMV-based system and Category merging
sections.summary: The suggestion to study an OMV-based system and merge Cat A and Cat B will be looked at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: First of all, I do confirm that indeed we will look specifically at Mr Chia's suggestion, which is to look at a system that is OMV-based, but also to look at merging Cat A and Cat B in a single-bidding category.

sections.label: HDB car park electrical upgrades
sections.summary: First phase of electrical upgrades for around 450 HDB multi-storey car parks is expected to complete by 2029.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the Member's second question, our constraint really is our electrical infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I would like share that we have kickstarted our first phase of upgrades, which would benefit around 450 HDB multi-storey car parks and this upgrade is expected to complete by around 2029.

sections.label: Maritime sector and GRIT programme
sections.summary: Young aspirants apply for jobs instead of traineeships, and the maritime sector has not participated in the GRIT programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: So, the natural thing to do for young aspirants is to apply for jobs instead of going through traineeship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: So, for the maritime sector, we have not participated in the GRIT programme.

sections.label: Fee review and RTS Link
sections.summary: LTA and MOT periodically review the fee and will raise it substantially from 2027, when the RTS Link opens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: LTA and MOT, we periodically review this fee, and in fact, we are going to raise the fee substantially from 2027 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: At the same time as when the RTS Link is open.

sections.label: Single deck and double deck buses
sections.summary: New electric single deck buses remain in Singapore, but double deck buses are preferred as more efficient and reducing reliance on bus captains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: So, that is why you have still fairly new electric single deck buses in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: But of course, we want to try to have double decks, high-capacity buses as much as we can, because they are the most efficient, space saving and reduces our reliance on bus captains, because one bus captain driving a double deck is much better than one bus captain driving a single deck.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: So, these are sort of the reasons that are hard to see on the outside, but I hope the Member and the public understands why you still see single decks on the roads today.

sections.label: Commuter education and construction disamenities
sections.summary: The Ministry will address commuter education on mutual respect and zero tolerance for aggressive behaviour, and recognises construction disamenities disrupting residents, commuters and motorists.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
sentences.text: As we promote the norm of asking, how will the Ministry also ensure that commuter education emphasises mutual respect and a zero tolerance for aggressive or entitled behaviour?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I will have to come back to her specifically on the timeline that she requested, but on the question she had about the disamenities that can be caused due to construction works, we definitely recognise this, that it disrupts residents, commuters, motorists as well.

sections.label: Covered linkways for condominiums
sections.summary: URA will work with LTA to require condominium developers to build covered linkways to transport nodes, with LTA providing linkways within transport nodes and discussing with stakeholders where land belongs to another agency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: If covered linkways are required to connect residents to nearby transport nodes, URA will work with LTA to impose requirements on the condominium developers to construct these covered workways as part of the planning approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I know that for existing condominiums or estates that were built before this requirement, there could be challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: And for LTA's planning, you might be aware that we already provide linkways, covered linkways within transport nodes, 400 metres, 800 metres within Friendly Streets and all these.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: But in areas where the land belongs to another agency, like PUB as in the case that he mentioned in his cut, LTA will help to discuss with the different stakeholders.

sections.label: Condominium linkway requirement
sections.summary: A particular condominium does not meet LTA's requirement because it lacks an internal sheltered linkway from the residential building to the side gate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: In the case of that particular condominium, I understand that the condominium does not currently meet the LTA's requirement because there is no internal sheltered linkway from the residential building to the side gate – so that must first be in place, before LTA can even think about joining it to a bus stop or transport node.
